worker_guidelines.title: What Yaadly is, and what you are agreeing to
worker_guidelines.html:
Yaadly connects vetted tradespeople with property owners, most of them overseas, and holds every job to one standard: work is proven with evidence, and money moves when the client approves that evidence. These guidelines are the rules of working with us. They exist to protect you as much as the client. Every rule here has a named counterpart on the other side, and nobody carries the risk alone.

What Yaadly charges you: 12% of your agreed labour price on a completed job, taken at the point you are paid, so you keep 88%. Remote digital work carries 10% instead. Materials are never charged a fee, at cost is at cost. What you never pay: joining is free, quoting is free, there are no lead fees whether you win the job or not, and there is no subscription.

Amended in v1.1. Version 1.0 stated that workers are never charged. That was wrong. It is corrected here rather than quietly, and no signature against v1.0 is carried over onto this wording, everyone re-signs.

worker_guidelines.title: Verification, before your first job
worker_guidelines.html:
Nobody attends a client property unverified. Before your first job you will show government photo ID on a video call, provide a live photo and a short video turning your face left to right, proof of address dated within three months, and your TRN. You give three references we will call, and you confirm each one has been told we are calling. Certified trades have their certification checked with the body that issued it.

Police record check, Jamaica Constabulary Force. Mandatory for any job over £500, any work inside an occupied home, and any job where you hold keys or attend an empty property. Optional below £500 with the owner present, and a client may still require it. Without a current check on file you cannot be matched to any job in the mandatory categories.

Your first job carries an independent reviewer on site, at Yaadly’s cost. They walk the work with you and their notes join the record. This is not a probation you can fail quietly, it is how a brand-new profile carries the same promise as a worker with thirty jobs behind them.

worker_guidelines.title: Quoting
worker_guidelines.html:
• You set your own price. Yaadly does not price your work and never shows you a band to quote against.
  • Quote labour separately from materials. The fee is calculated on labour only.
  • Name your exclusions in writing. What you leave out of the quote is what you are not being paid for, and it is what stops an argument in a fortnight.
  • Quoting is free, every time, win or lose. There is no lead fee on this platform.

worker_guidelines.title: On site: conduct
worker_guidelines.html:
• Turn up when you said, or say so before the day, not on it.
  • Treat the client, their family and anyone giving you access with respect. They see your conduct the way you see theirs.
  • Extra work found on site is raised through Yaadly with a photo and a price before it is done. Unagreed work is not payable, which protects you as much as them.
  • Never ask for a side payment and never accept one. It voids the protection for both of you.
  • Leave the site clean and show the waste has gone.

Materials on site

  • Materials go where the client said, and nowhere else. The client names the place before you are paid to buy anything. Film them in that exact place with the receipt and file it as materials on site.
  • That filing is what moves the risk in them to the client. Do it and a theft afterwards is the client’s loss, not yours. Fail to do it, keep them somewhere else, or leave them plainly insecure, and the risk stays with you. This is the one place on this platform where a photograph is worth actual money to you.
  • Your tools are your own risk, always. Stored, filmed, locked up or not. No client is ever responsible for your drill.
  • Where the property has nowhere securable, you buy in drops sized to the next stage and take the surplus away each night. Price those trips into your quote, because they are real work and they are not paid for afterwards.

Added in v1.3. This is not the usual arrangement in construction, where unfixed materials stay the contractor’s risk. Here the client names the place and your evidence moves the risk across. It is better for you than the trade default, and only if you file the evidence.

worker_guidelines.title: Evidence: how your work gets proven
worker_guidelines.html:
Every stage has a checklist issued in the Kickoff Pack or Job Sheet. You file evidence against it and you write no paperwork. Evidence is timestamped and fingerprinted on upload, that is what makes it proof rather than photographs.

  • Document the site on arrival, before anything is touched.
  • Photograph materials with the receipt, in the place the client named for them, and file it as materials on site. See section 4.
  • Nothing gets covered over before it has been photographed.
  • Evidence from another job, reused, is a permanent removal. There is no second version of that conversation.

worker_guidelines.title: The Completion Report and your Yaad Score
worker_guidelines.html: At the end of the job a Completion Report is drafted for you from your evidence. You read it and confirm one thing: what is written is what was done. Signing something untrue is treated the same as a false document. Every completed, documented job builds your Yaad Score, a verified record you own, that counts with clients and, in time, with a bank.

worker_guidelines.title: Getting paid
worker_guidelines.html:
• Yaadly is not holding money at present. Your labour is paid by the client through the route agreed on your job. Said plainly, because you are entitled to know it before you turn up: Yaadly cannot pay you if the client does not. When holding goes live this section changes and you will be asked to re-sign it.
  • A “Yaadly payment link” for your labour during this period did not come from Yaadly. Send it to us before you touch it.
  • Materials are paid against your receipt before the labour stages run, and are never charged a fee on either side.
  • Once your evidence is in and the client approves, you are paid within 3 working days: bank transfer, Lynk wallet or remittance pick-up, whichever you chose.
  • You can see what you are owed and what has been paid in your worker portal.
  • Payment is per stage, not one lump at the end. A stage signed off is a stage paid.

Corrected in v1.3. Version 1.2 told you the client’s payment was “confirmed and held before you start.” That was not true, because holding is not switched on yet, and it was the sentence most likely to be relied on. Corrected here rather than quietly.

worker_guidelines.title: If something goes wrong
worker_guidelines.html:
Disputes are reviewed by a person, not an algorithm, and they are free. You are the first point of contact, most things are a misunderstanding and get fixed in a day. If that does not resolve it, it escalates to Yaadly: a person reads the whole thread as it stands, neither side rewrites it, and nothing is released while it is open.

Site visits during a dispute. Where a dispute needs eyes on site, Yaadly attends for a visual review only, we look, we record what we see, we do not certify and we do not adjudicate the trade craft. One visit is covered. Any further site visit is chargeable, because it was not agreed at the start of the job.

client_guidelines.title: What being a Yaadly client means
client_guidelines.html: Yaadly gets property work done on evidence: verified workers, documented stages, and money that moves only when you approve what you can see. These guidelines are your side of that deal. Every protection you enjoy has a named counterpart the worker enjoys, and nobody carries the risk alone.

client_guidelines.title: Describing your job honestly
client_guidelines.html:
• Describe the site and the work as they really are. Workers can walk away from a mis-described site without penalty, so an honest pitch protects your own timeline.
  • Share what you know: access, occupancy, past repairs, anything already tried or quoted.
  • Your job card fields are what workers filter on. A blank field is a job that never reaches the right person.

client_guidelines.title: Quotes and choosing
client_guidelines.html:
• Workers quote their own price. Yaadly does not price work and does not publish a band for a job type, we do project management and oversight, not price estimation.
  • Your own budget band is never shown to a worker. It exists so we can tell you early if what you want and what you have are not the same thing.
  • Do not beat workers down or ask them to shave the price off-platform. A fair yes or a clean no.
  • All work is engaged through Yaadly. Approaching a worker from this platform for a side deal removes the protection for both of you, and repeat side-dealing ends the account.

client_guidelines.title: While the work runs
client_guidelines.html:
• Keep the access you promised. If your ground contact cannot open up on an agreed day, say so the day before.
  • Treat workers with respect, in messages and in person. They are verified professionals, and they see your conduct the way you see theirs.
  • Extra work you think of on site goes through Yaadly first, in writing, never negotiated at the gate.

Materials on your property

  • You say where materials are to be kept on the property, and nothing is released to buy them until you have. This is a question we will ask you, and the system will not let the money move without an answer.
  • The worker then photographs and films the materials in the place you named, with the receipt. From the moment that evidence is filed the materials are yours and at your risk, because you chose the place and it is your property. If he keeps them somewhere else, or leaves them plainly insecure, the risk stays with him. His own tools are his risk in every case.
  • Check that your property insurance covers materials on site before work starts. Many policies do not, and cover on an unoccupied house is usually the most restricted of all. This is the single thing on this page most worth ten minutes of your time.
  • If there is nowhere securable, say so. That is a real answer, not a failure. The worker then buys in drops sized to the next stage and takes the surplus away each night, priced into his quote up front. Nothing is left overnight, so nothing passes to you.
  • Yaadly is not your insurer and holds no cover for your materials. If they are stolen after that evidence is filed, the loss is yours. Where it happens we will contribute up to half the documented value of what was taken, capped at £150, once per job, as a goodwill payment and not as an entitlement. It comes from a goodwill line funded out of our own fees, separate from the Guarantee. It is not cover, and it is not a substitute for the paragraph above.

Added in v1.3. Who carries materials on site was not written down anywhere before this. It is written here because it is not the usual arrangement in construction, and nobody should discover that after a theft.

client_guidelines.title: Evidence, approval and money
client_guidelines.html:
• Review evidence when it lands, within 3 days where you can. A worker who has proven a stage is waiting on your word to be paid.
  • At sign-off you may approve from the evidence, book a live video walkthrough, or book an independent reviewer to attend the site, see section 6.
  • Approve when the evidence shows the agreed work; raise it before you approve when it does not. Disputes are free and reviewed by a person, and nothing moves while one is open.
  • Yaadly’s Guarantee & Support fee is 15% of the worker’s labour price, in the headline total, never charged on materials, subject to a small-job minimum of J$3,500 to J$4,500 by trade. It is itemised before you agree to anything. Where you pay in a currency other than Jamaican dollars, the conversion carries a margin of about 2%.
  • Pay through the route agreed for your job. While Yaadly is not holding money, paying your tradesperson directly is that route, and it is not going behind our backs. What it does mean is plain: Yaadly is holding nothing on your job, so Yaadly can withhold nothing, release nothing and return nothing. Never withhold approval to renegotiate a price already agreed.

Corrected in v1.3. Version 1.2 said “never pay a worker directly on the side” while paying your tradesperson directly was, and is, exactly how a job runs today. The rule described a way of working that is not switched on yet.

Added in v1.1. Version 1.0 carried no fee clause at all, and clients signed it. This is the correction.

client_guidelines.title: Independent review at sign-off
client_guidelines.html:
You may have somebody attend the property before you release the final payment. Two levels, chosen when the job is set up and priced then, not after:

  • Visual Check, £149 (£95 founding). A trained checker attends, records the finished work against the agreed scope, photographs anything visibly wrong, and files a one-page observation note in 72 hours. They record. They do not rate, advise or certify. Mirrors the UK property inspection report at £80 to 150.
  • Condition Report, £325 (£245 founding). The whole property recorded system by system, every finding rated Severe, Moderate or Low, issue summary on page one. Mirrors a RICS Level 1 at £300 to 900, it tells you what is wrong and how bad, not what to do about it.
  • Technical Sign-off, £300 (£245 founding, £395 inside 48 hours). A qualified trade inspector assesses one stage against the trade standard and gives you a pass, a fail, or a written list of what to put right. The first rung that gives an opinion. Priced against a UK structural engineer’s site visit at £300.

Live viewing, £40, on any rung. By default the inspection happens and you get the report afterwards. If you would rather be there, we call you in on video while the inspector is on site: you see what they see, you can ask them to look closer at something, and anything you raise goes in the report as your own note.

Every rung is priced at or below the bottom of its UK band, because the scope is narrower, one property or one works package, not a whole pre-purchase survey. A checker records. A trained inspector advises. We tell you which one you are buying before you buy it.

Visits not agreed at the start are chargeable. Where a dispute is raised we will attend for a visual review, and one visit is covered. Any further visit is charged, because it was not in the scope you agreed. We attend to look and record, certification is a matter for a PERB-registered engineer, and we will say so rather than guess.

completion_section6:
6 \u00b7 What this report is not

A record of physical works and costs, prepared by a construction project manager. Nothing in it is legal advice or a legal opinion. No title verified, no agreement interpreted, no boundary identified, no structure certified, those are matters for an attorney-at-law, a commissioned land surveyor and a PERB-registered engineer respectively. Findings are limited to what was visible and accessible on the dates stated.

We carried out this service with reasonable care and skill, as section 49 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 requires. Nothing here limits that duty or your rights under it.
